source: Gu, Wang, Zhang, Li (2025) LLMs can realize combinatorial creativity (arXiv 2412.14141)
finding: Framework that implements Boden-style combinational creativity with an LLM: retrieve ideas from other domains at four abstraction levels (L1 domain-specific to L4 universal), then break each into components and recombine them.
numbers: Backbone Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Retrieval by OpenAI text-embedding-3-large cosine similarity, matched per generalization level L1-L4. Each stored innovation also has universal_principle, key_mechanism, domain_agnostic_reframing, design_rationale, key_tradeoffs.
quote: The retrieval system maps concepts across different abstraction levels to enable meaningful connections between disparate domains
limits: Design paper; the retrieval-by-abstraction step is the part that targets distant domains.
agent_relevance: Direct analogue of O7: pull a source by its abstract principle, not its surface words, then decompose into components and recombine.

source: Gu, Wang, Zhang, Li (2025) LLMs can realize combinatorial creativity (arXiv 2412.14141)
finding: Main result: generated ideas were closer to the real paper's innovation than a no-retrieval baseline.
numbers: 87 OAG-Bench papers, 3-5 key references each. SPECTER cosine similarity: DR-Sim 0.85 vs 0.78, UP-Sim 0.83 vs 0.75, KM-Sim 0.87 vs 0.77. Abstract claims +7% to +10%.
limits: Confound: the framework is given the paper's own key references as its knowledge base; the baseline gets only the problem statement. No ablation of retrieval vs decomposition. No human rating, no significance test, one model. SPECTER similarity to a known paper rewards re-inventing, not novelty.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence. It shows that supplying the right source plus a decompose-and-recombine step helps recover a known idea; it does not show distant sources beat near ones.

source: Gu, Wang, Zhang, Li (2025) LLMs can realize combinatorial creativity (arXiv 2412.14141)
finding: Qualitative check on 3 cases (decoupled weight decay for adaptive optimizers, three-stream text matching, Bayesian cold-start active learning): generated ideas judged near-identical to the real ones in core mechanism.
numbers: 3 cases out of 87; judged by the authors, no blind raters.
limits: Author-judged; cases chosen by the authors; the references contain the needed pieces.
agent_relevance: Combining given pieces works when the pieces are in the pool. The hard part for our agent is choosing the pool.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans, KOMBINE (arXiv 2509.21043)
finding: First open-ended benchmark for the three forms of combinatorial creativity: association (Mednick), analogy (Gentner), blending (Fauconnier-Turner), on random entity pairs with no known link (e.g. blue whale and mattress). Scores utility, surprise, originality; originality is mean embedding distance to the 5 nearest answers other responders gave for the same item.
numbers: 35 LLMs at temperature 0.9. Entities sampled from Wikidata with at least 78 sitelinks. Judges: Claude Haiku 4.5 (facts), panel of 3 LLMs (analogy and blend). Judge-human agreement 75% on items where the panel is unanimous.
limits: LLM judges; originality is relative to the pool of responders; embedder all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (authors report robustness across embedders).
agent_relevance: A scoring recipe to copy for O7 tests: validity gate first (utility 0/1), then distance-based surprise and pool-relative originality.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans, KOMBINE (arXiv 2509.21043)
finding: Blending is hardest; the bottleneck is finding the shared abstraction (generic space), not building the blend.
numbers: Averaged over 35 LLMs: factual association 59.0%, valid analogy 53.4%, valid blend 43.4%. Given a valid generic space, a coherent blend followed 97.1% of the time. Best overall gpt-5.6-sol 55.2; best association claude-opus-4.6 51.4; analogy claude-opus-4.6 63.1; blending gpt-5.6-sol 64.8. Every entity pair had at least one model find a valid blend.
quote: models can find a generic space only 43.4% of the time on average
limits: Model names as printed in the paper; one run per item. Gaps between top models are small.
agent_relevance: Supports our design: verify the shared abstraction in code or by a check, because everything after it is cheap.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans, KOMBINE (arXiv 2509.21043)
finding: Inventive homogeneity: different LLMs invent the same concept for the same input pair.
numbers: 2,070 invented concepts, 7,868 properties; similarity threshold cos 0.674 (99th percentile of property pairs). 19.9% (412/2,070) share at least 2 near-identical properties with another model's concept. Same-family excess over cross-provider rate: DeepSeek +12.2 pp, Anthropic +11.1 pp, xAI +7.4, Meta +4.2, Qwen +2.6, Z.ai +1.2, Google +0.4, OpenAI -1.4. A task split (blends higher than analogies, 37.3% vs 2.6% at one setting) is read from a partly garbled figure.
limits: The threshold choice drives the headline rate; the task split is uncertain from the extraction.
agent_relevance: Supports G4: even different models are not independent in what they invent. Do not count agreement as validation of a novel combination.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans, KOMBINE (arXiv 2509.21043)
finding: Humans score below nearly every LLM, mostly because humans fail the validity gate. Humans and LLMs use different regions of concept space.
numbers: 75 Prolific adults (from 120 recruited, screened for AI use), 5 items per task. Valid or factual: association 22.1% (LLM 59.0%), analogy 32.9% (53.4%), blend 12.8% (43.4%). Overall score humans 13.7 vs best LLM 55.2. LLMs name people and places (+5.2 pp, +3.6 pp); humans use everyday objects and motion verbs (+7.6 pp).
limits: Online sample; skipped items scored zero, which pushes human scores down. LLM judges.
agent_relevance: A second source of diversity (a different corpus or human input) may add what same-model sampling cannot.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) Measuring combinatorial creativity in LLMs and humans, KOMBINE (arXiv 2509.21043)
finding: Originality of far association predicts originality and validity of analogies and blends across models.
numbers: Across 35 models: association originality vs analogy originality r=0.73, analogy surprise r=0.63, blend originality r=0.42, blend surprise r=0.50, valid blends r=0.48. Task-score correlations: association-analogy r=0.71, analogy-blending 0.70, blending-association 0.54.
limits: Correlational across models, not causal.
agent_relevance: A cheap far-association probe may be a usable proxy for a model's ability at O7.

source: Nagarajan, Wu, Ding, Raghunathan (2025) Roll the dice and look before you leap, ICML (arXiv 2504.15266)
finding: Minimal algorithmic tasks for combinational creativity (sibling discovery, triangle discovery: find new links in a stored knowledge graph) show next-token training is myopic; multi-token training gives more diverse and original outputs.
numbers: Gemma v1 2B: about 5x higher algorithmic creativity (valid, novel, unique outputs) under multi-token teacherless or diffusion training on the discovery tasks. Seed-conditioning (random prefix at the input) matched or beat temperature sampling for diversity.
quote: next-token learning is myopic; multi-token approaches comparatively excel in producing diverse and original output
limits: Toy graphs, fine-tuned small model, not a prompted frontier model; loose abstraction of a creative leap.
agent_relevance: Randomness should enter before the model plans the combination (a randomly drawn source chosen in code), not only at token sampling.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs generate novel research ideas? (arXiv 2409.04109)
finding: Blind expert review: LLM ideas rated more novel than expert ideas.
numbers: 79 reviewers, 49 ideas per condition, 3 conditions. Novelty (reviews as datapoints): human 4.84 (N=119 reviews), AI 5.64 (N=109, p<0.01), AI reranked by a human 5.81 (p<0.001). Excitement: AI 5.19 (p<0.05), AI reranked 5.46 (p<0.01). Feasibility: AI 6.34, no significant difference. Held under Bonferroni correction and mixed-effects models.
limits: Novelty rated by humans, noisy. Only 7 NLP topics. The ideas came from an LLM pipeline with paper retrieval, overgeneration and ranking.
agent_relevance: Ideation novelty is easy to get; see the duplicate plateau and the execution gap below.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) arXiv 2409.04109
finding: Generating more ideas does not give more distinct ideas: duplicates pile up. LLM judges are weak at ranking ideas.
numbers: Of 4,000 generated seed ideas per topic, only about 200 were non-duplicates (cosine above 0.8 on all-MiniLM-L6-v2 counted as duplicate). The share of new non-duplicates per batch falls and accumulated unique ideas plateau. LLM judging of accepted vs rejected papers: best 71.4% (Claude-3.5-Sonnet), GPT-4o 61.1%, Claude-3-Opus 63.5%.
limits: Threshold 0.8 chosen by manual inspection.
agent_relevance: Brute-force sampling saturates. Dedup in code and diversify by changing the source concept, not by resampling.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The ideation-execution gap (arXiv 2506.20803)
finding: When the same ideas were executed, LLM ideas lost far more than human ideas, closing the novelty advantage.
numbers: 43 experts each spent over 100 hours executing a randomly assigned idea; 58 blind reviewers. Score change after execution, human vs AI: novelty -0.010 vs -1.049; excitement 0.078 vs -1.760; effectiveness -0.052 vs -1.879; overall -0.628 vs -1.976. Difference (human minus AI): 1.039 (p=0.025), 1.835 (p=0.001), 1.827 (p=0.003), 1.348 (p=0.004), FDR corrected.
limits: N=43 projects, NLP prompting topics only, three-month window.
agent_relevance: A combination that reads as novel may not survive running it. Test by execution (G3).

source: Wang, Downey, Ji, Hope (2023/2024) SciMON (arXiv 2305.14259)
finding: Retrieves 'inspirations' (semantic neighbors, KG neighbors, citation neighbors) plus an iterative retrieve-compare-update loop to boost novelty.
numbers: Study I: 6 NLP experts, 50 instances; GPT-4 few-shot rated far above GPT-3.5 variants (GPT-3.5 few-shot 33% helpful). Study II: versus real paper ideas, the real idea had higher technical level and novelty in 85% of comparisons. Study III: 70 instances, 5 annotators: first novelty iteration changed 88.9% of ideas substantially and raised novelty in 55.6%; second iteration raised it for 57.8% of continued ideas; no drops.
quote: the model often tends to suggest combinations between popular concepts
limits: Small human studies; annotator agreement 43.8-75% in Study I. Authors note the model tends to combine popular concepts, so the boost stays in the popular region.
agent_relevance: Iterating against retrieved prior work is a code-checkable novelty test. Combining popular concepts is the default failure.

source: Hope, Chan, Kittur, Shahaf (2017) Accelerating innovation through analogy mining, KDD (arXiv 1706.05585)
finding: Retrieve analogies by purpose and mechanism (same purpose, different mechanism) rather than surface text. In an ideation experiment such inspirations roughly doubled the chance of a good idea.
numbers: Corpus: Quirky product descriptions with crowd purpose/mechanism labels; training about 5,500 products, test N=2,500 pairs. Ideation: 38 AMT workers, within-subject, 12 seed products, 749 ideas. P(good idea), k=2 raters: analogy 0.71 [0.48,0.87] vs TF-IDF 0.28 [0.16,0.44] vs random 0.27 [0.16,0.41]; k=3: 0.56 vs 0.16 vs 0.14 (all p<.01).
limits: Wide CIs (authors say a replication may give a smaller effect). Inspiration shown after one minute of unaided ideation.
agent_relevance: Best human evidence that mechanism-distance with matched purpose beats surface similarity: a retrieval rule our O7 can copy.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs, Nature Human Behaviour (arXiv 2212.09196)
finding: GPT-3 matched or beat college students on text matrix, letter-string and verbal analogies, zero-shot.
numbers: Digit Matrices: GPT-3 beat humans (N=40) on generative accuracy, OR 1.88, 95% CI [1.21,2.91], p=0.005. Letter strings: humans N=57. Story analogies (Gentner materials, humans N=54): humans clearly better, OR 0.37 [0.21,0.63], p=0.0003; GPT-3 weak on far analogies, GPT-4 preliminarily better.
limits: Contested; see the counterfactual failure. Verbal analogies may be in training data.
agent_relevance: LLMs can map structure when relations are familiar; far, unfamiliar analogy is the weak spot.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Counterfactual tasks for analogical reasoning in LLMs (arXiv 2402.08955)
finding: Failed generalisation of the Webb result: on letter-string analogies with permuted alphabets, GPT accuracy drops sharply while humans stay steady.
numbers: Counterfactual alphabets, 1,876 human samples and 6,840 per model: accuracy humans 0.753 [0.734,0.773], GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452. Models passed a comprehension check of the new alphabets.
quote: the GPT models' performance declines sharply on the counterfactual set
limits: One task family; later models not tested.
agent_relevance: Do not trust the model's own analogical mapping on unfamiliar structure; verify the mapping by a check (G3).

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners, ICLR (arXiv 2310.01714)
finding: Prompting the model to recall relevant past problems and knowledge before solving ('self-generated exemplars') beats 0-shot and few-shot CoT.
numbers: Abstract: average gain about +4%. GSM8K GPT-3.5-turbo about 75-78%; MATH GPT-3.5-turbo up to 37.3% (table extraction garbled; direction certain, row mapping not). Codeforces: GPT-3.5-turbo-16k Acc@1 15% vs GPT-4 baseline 16%; GPT-4 Acc@10 up to 37%.
limits: Analogy here is same-domain recall, not distant. Exact per-row numbers uncertain.
agent_relevance: A cheap O7-like step (recall similar solved problems) works but is near-domain; not distant combination.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2024) Divergent creativity in humans and LLMs (arXiv 2405.13012)
finding: Far-word association (Divergent Association Task) compared across LLMs and about 100,000 humans.
numbers: GPT-4 above human mean (significant); Gemini Pro not different from humans; GPT-4-turbo scored lower than GPT-4; GPT-4 DAT rose with temperature, mean 85.6 at the highest temperature, above 72% of human scores. Top human decile beats every model.
limits: DAT checks word distance only, not value. Schapiro et al. note poor external validity of DAT for real creative tasks.
agent_relevance: Word-level distance is easy for LLMs; value and validity are the hard part.

source: Sourati and Evans (2023) Accelerating science with human-aware AI (arXiv 2306.01495)
finding: Models that include who researches what predict future discoveries up to 400% better than content-only models, and can be steered away from the crowd to propose 'alien' hypotheses.
numbers: Test beds: about 1.5M materials articles (1937-2018) and MEDLINE drug repurposing of about 4K drugs against 100 diseases; prediction year 2001 (materials), 2020 (COVID). Gains largest where literature is sparse.
limits: Retrodictive tests; 'alien' hypotheses unvalidated. Not an LLM scaffold.
agent_relevance: Combinations the crowd is unlikely to try are the unexplored ones; keep a counted list of pairs already tried and avoid them.

source: Uzzi, Mukherjee, Stringer, Jones (2013) Atypical combinations and scientific impact, Science 342:468
finding: Founding large-scale test: the highest-impact papers combine mostly conventional prior work with a small dose of atypical combinations; the most novel papers are not the highest-impact.
numbers: 17.9 million papers, Web of Science, five decades. Crossref record: cited by 1,272 items.
quote: The highest-impact papers were not the ones that had the greatest novelty
limits: Only the Crossref record was read, not the full paper, so exact hit-rate figures are not recorded here. Journal-pair citation links as the unit of combination.
agent_relevance: Supports a conservative mix: mostly familiar structure plus one distant element, not maximum distance.

source: Uzzi et al. (2013) full-paper figures, recalled
finding: Recalled, not opened: papers with a median conventional combination plus a high tail of atypical combinations were about twice as likely to be in the top 5% most cited, fewer than 10% of papers had that profile.
numbers: Recalled approximate figures only; verify before use.
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Verify in a later pass before relying on the 2x figure.

source: Computational creativity (Wikipedia, secondary; Boden, Wiggins, Veale, Falkenhainer)
finding: Boden's view: a great deal, perhaps all, of human creativity is novel combination of existing ideas. Computational models: conceptual integration networks, Veale and O'Donoghue 2007 (blending via analogy mapping), Pereira 2006 (symbolic AI plus genetic algorithms), SME (Falkenhainer, Forbus, Gentner 1989), MAC/FAC, ACME, ARCS, Sapper.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Secondary source; page read only to character 100,000. Wiggins (2006) formalised Boden mostly as a touchstone.
agent_relevance: Retrieval (MAC/FAC) and mapping (SME) are the two stages our O7 needs.

source: Fauconnier and Turner conceptual blending (Wikipedia, secondary)
finding: Blending theory: two input spaces, a generic space of shared structure, selective projection into a blend with emergent structure (composition, completion, elaboration).
numbers: No experiments on the page.
limits: Critics: Gibbs (2000) says it lacks testable hypotheses; Ritchie (2004) says many blends reduce to simpler processes; the theory does not say where the inputs come from.
agent_relevance: KOMBINE turns it into a scored task; a valid generic space is the measurable step.

source: Structure-mapping theory (Wikipedia, secondary; Gentner 1983)
finding: Analogy transfers relations, not attributes; systematicity: predicates in a connected relational system are more likely mapped. Steps: alignment, inference, evaluation.
numbers: Time pressure and high working-memory load push people to surface object matches.
limits: No numbers on page; competitor: Tversky contrast theory counts shared attributes.
agent_relevance: Gives the O7 check: accept a mapping only if relations (not surface features) align and the projected inference is tested.

source: Remote Associates Test (Wikipedia, secondary; Mednick 1962)
finding: Mednick: creativity is forming associative elements into new combinations that meet requirements; the more remote the elements, the more creative the result. RAT: 30 items, 40 minutes, find the fourth word linking three.
numbers: Mednick reported Spearman-Brown reliability 0.92 (women's college sample) and 0.91 (Michigan men). Bowden and Jung-Beeman (2003): 144 compound items.
limits: Weak validity: no data that high scorers excel in any field; Worthen and Clark (1971) said it measures language sensitivity; now treated as a convergent-thinking or insight task.
agent_relevance: Remoteness alone is not value; tie any distance measure to a validity gate.

source: Koestler (1964) The Act of Creation, bisociation (Wikipedia, secondary)
finding: Every creative act is bisociation: two frames ('matrices') incompatible by habit are joined; covers humour, science and art; breakthroughs often follow effort then relaxation.
numbers: No numbers or tests on the page.
limits: No empirical test or critique listed.
agent_relevance: Conceptual root of O7; no evidence beyond case histories.

source: Hadamard (1954) and Einstein's 'combinatory play' (quoted in Schapiro et al.)
finding: Introspective reports of mathematicians and scientists describe invention as combining ideas; Einstein: combinatory play is the essential feature of productive thought.
numbers: Anecdotal, no numbers.
limits: Introspection; selection bias.
agent_relevance: Motivating anecdotes only.

source: Shi and Evans (2023) Surprising combinations of research contents and contexts, Nature Communications (cited in KOMBINE)
finding: As cited in Schapiro et al.: highly impactful scholarly work tends to comprise more distant combinations of ideas, methods and concepts, and surprising combinations emerge with scientists from distant disciplines.
numbers: Numbers not read.
limits: Known only via citation in an opened paper; primary not opened.
agent_relevance: Open in a later pass; it partly conflicts with Uzzi's 'mostly conventional' finding, so the distance optimum is unsettled.
